source.publication: 2025 Oklahoma Resident Individual Income Tax Forms and Instructions (Form 511 packet)
source.section: Form 511 lines 1-14 and 18 (PDF pages 42-43); select line instructions (PDF pages 9-10); standard deduction line 10 (PDF page 10); exemptions line 11 and the Regular exemption terms (PDF pages 8 and 10); Tax Table (PDF pages 27-38); Schedule 511-A (form PDF page 45); Schedule 511-A line 5, Oklahoma Government or Federal Civil Service Retirement (PDF page 17); Schedule 511-A line 6, Other Retirement Income (PDF page 17)

worked: Federal AGI = wages (you) 30,000.00 + Oklahoma public pension (you) 12,000.00 + IRA distribution (spouse) 12,000.00 = 54,000.00. Federal taxable income = 54,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 22,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Oklahoma starts from federal AGI). Schedule 511-A: line 5: you 12,000.00 in federal AGI, limit 10,000.00, claims 10,000.00; line total 10,000.00; line 6: spouse 12,000.00 in federal AGI, limit 10,000.00 - 0.00 on line 5 = 10,000.00, claims 10,000.00; line total 10,000.00; line 18 total subtractions 10,000.00 + 10,000.00 = 20,000.00. Form 511: line 1 federal AGI 54,000.00; line 2 subtractions 20,000.00; line 3 = 54,000.00 - 20,000.00 = 34,000.00; line 4 out-of-state income 0.00; line 5 34,000.00; line 6 additions 0.00; line 7 Oklahoma AGI 34,000.00; line 8 adjustments 0.00; line 9 34,000.00; line 10 standard deduction (married joint) 12,700.00; line 11 exemptions: 2 Regular + 0 Special = 2 x 1,000.00 = 2,000.00 (no one is 65 or older, 0 Special); line 12 = 12,700.00 + 2,000.00 = 14,700.00; line 13 taxable income = 34,000.00 - 14,700.00 = 19,300.00; line 14 tax (the projection's brackets as numbers; the booklet prints only a table and worksheets): 0.25% x 2,000.00 = 5.0000 + 0.75% x 3,000.00 = 22.5000 + 1.75% x 2,500.00 = 43.7500 + 2.75% x 2,300.00 = 63.2500 + 3.75% x 4,600.00 = 172.5000 + 4.75% x 4,900.00 = 232.7500; total 539.7500 = 539.75. Line 13 is under 100,000, so the form reads the tax table: row 19,300-19,350, column 'Married filing joint or head of household', PDF page 29, gives 541; expected keeps the schedule figure. Lines 15-17 credits 0.00; line 18 income tax 539.75. The limit is per person: your line 5 claim does not reduce your spouse's line 6 limit.
accepted_approximations: The brackets are derived from the printed tax table and the 100,000-and-over worksheets; the booklet prints no schedule. Below 100,000 tax is figured on the exact income, where the booklet taxes each 50-dollar row at its midpoint and rounds. At 100,000 and over the single and separate worksheet starts from 4,562 where the schedule gives 4,561.50.

Lines 5 and 6 share one 10,000 limit per person. It is written as the line 6 cap reduced by the person's public pension, which gives the same result as the booklet's '10,000 minus the amounts already claimed on line 5' when every public pension is on the line 5 list.
